claims.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
Pulumi Policy as Code (via `@pulumi/policy`'s `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`) can implement infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi.
Pulumi's Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic, programmatic infrastructure management.
The Pulumi Automation API is imported via `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes `pulumi.LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` to create or select a stack.
Pulumi component resources can be created that integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, hiding multi-tool management complexity from development teams.
Pulumi component resources are created by extending the `pulumi.ComponentResource` class.

The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide (this guide series) teaches referencing existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, using any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, importing and using Terraform modules directly, converting HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrating both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Pulumi can reference existing Terraform state files.
Pulumi can use any Terraform provider within Pulumi programs.
Pulumi can import and use Terraform modules directly.
Pulumi supports converting HCL code to Pulumi code when beneficial.
Pulumi can orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.

There exists a `terraform.state.S3Reference` construct/API in the Pulumi ecosystem (`@pulumi/terraform`) used to reference Terraform state stored in S3, with a `getOutput` method for retrieving state outputs.
Pulumi provides a `pulumi.StackReference` construct with a `getOutput` method to reference outputs from another stack.
